newsitem.title: UK: New Manchester runway due to be in service by 2000.
newsitem.headline: New Manchester runway due to be in service by 2000.

text.p: The government on Wednesday confirmed that it had approved planning permission for a second runway at Manchester airport, in north west England.

Transport Secretary Sir George Young said the 3,050 metre runway, due to come into operation in 2000, would enable Manchester airport to handle 63 aircraft movements an hour compared with 45 it can take now in peak periods.

"Passenger demand will outstrip existing runway capacity in the next few years at Manchester. A second runway will allow this growing demand to be met there, to the benefit of business and leisure passengers alike," he said in a statement.
Young said the second runway would also help to relieve capacity constraints at airports in southeast England.
The runway is the first full length runway to be built in Britain for 20 years.
